findings.failing_input: paginate() loops with MAX_CHUNKS=50 (50k row ceiling). If a real query returns exactly chunkSize rows on chunk 50 (50000 total), the loop breaks at MAX_CHUNKS WITHOUT detecting that more data exists. Silent truncation — no log, no warning. For data_daily with 3 stores × 365 days = 1095 rows, far below ceiling. But for a tail-end consumer (e.g. orders_attribution running for a year × hundreds of orders/day) this could clip.
findings.expected: On reaching MAX_CHUNKS with a full last chunk, emit a console.warn so the operator sees the cap was hit.
findings.actual: Silent truncation; downstream sees only first 50k rows.
findings.fix_sketch: if (chunk === MAX_CHUNKS - 1 && data.length === chunkSize) console.warn(`paginate(): hit MAX_CHUNKS=${MAX_CHUNKS} cap; data may be truncated`);
findings.regression_test_idea: Mock query to return exactly chunkSize rows on every iteration; advance to chunk 50; assert a console.warn was emitted.

findings.failing_input: data_daily row with total_spend_cad=0 explicitly (cron-daily writes 0 when no spend) AND fb+ga+tt all 0. The current code: totalSpend = toNumber(0) || fbSpend+gaSpend+ttSpend → 0 || 0 → 0 (correct). But: totalSpend=0 AND fb+ga+tt=200 → toNumber(0) || 200 → 0 || 200 → 200. This OVERRIDES a stored 0 with the sum, which is wrong if the writer intentionally stored 0 (meaning 'truly no spend confirmed') vs ‘missing’. Today the writer doesn't distinguish but the || fallback uses 0 as 'missing'.
findings.expected: Use explicit null check: totalSpendRaw == null ? sum : toNumber(totalSpendRaw). Already done on line 298 — but line 300 then does `|| fbSpend+gaSpend+ttSpend` which kicks in for any 0 value.
findings.actual: Stored value of 0 is treated as missing and replaced with sum-of-parts.
findings.fix_sketch: Remove the `|| fbSpend + gaSpend + ttSpend` tail on line 300; the null check on 298 already correctly handles the missing case.
findings.regression_test_idea: Insert row with total_spend_cad=0 AND fb_spend_cad=100; assert returned totalSpend===0 (currently returns 100).

findings.failing_input: STORE_NAME_BY_ID is hardcoded with 3 store IDs. If a new 4th store is onboarded but this map isn't updated, fetchCampaignsFromPostgres / fetchAdsFromPostgres / fetchOrdersAttributionFromPostgres / fetchProductCatalogFromPostgres all fallback storeName to storeId (line 661, 740, 814, 868) — UI shows the ID instead of the name.
findings.expected: Derive store names from a single shared source (e.g. fetchStoreMetaFromPostgres) or read from stores table once.
findings.actual: Hardcoded duplicate of campaigns.ts:38; drift risk.
findings.fix_sketch: Centralize in a shared module or lazy-fetch from stores table on first invocation; cache for process lifetime.
findings.regression_test_idea: Insert a row with store_id='newStore'; assert storeName === 'newStore' is acceptable fallback (not crash), and add lint to remind on map update.

findings.failing_input: Newest-row dedup uses string comparison: `updatedAt < prevAt`. Works for ISO-8601 UTC `Z` strings (tested explicitly). If a row ever has `updated_at` as TIMESTAMPTZ without Z suffix (e.g. '2026-05-23 11:00:00+00'), the comparison would still likely sort correctly but is fragile.
findings.expected: Parse with Date.parse and compare numerically; pin invariant in fixture.
findings.actual: String compare works for current schema but is forward-fragile.
findings.fix_sketch: const prevTs = Date.parse(prevAt); const curTs = Date.parse(updatedAt); if (Number.isFinite(prevTs) && Number.isFinite(curTs) && curTs < prevTs) continue;
findings.regression_test_idea: Insert mixed-format timestamps (with and without Z); assert newer wins regardless.

uncertainty_notes: All Phase 9 concerns addressed: C-02 (newest-row dedup) now has a dedicated test file with 5 cases, U-01 (TikTok writer↔reader symmetry) is fixed via shared TIKTOK_ACTIVE_ENOUGH from platformConfig.ts (line 44 import). Phase 11 relocation of StoreMetaRow from sheets.ts to here (line 361) is clean. Range filter is server-side. Pagination caps at 50k rows. Findings above are MINOR (current data volumes well below caps; current writers always produce UTC Z strings).
